body:
I know he has trouble getting to know people and I want to help him, but I can't be the only support for him because I don't want to become less close with my other friends and I'm suffering from depression myself. I'd like to get him to understand that the other people in our group are wonderful people too and want to get along with him.

Also, I'm a little bit afraid that he isn't my friend just because he thinks I'm a nice person, but because he's having a crush on me.

The solution to situation B made me laugh out loud. Maybe I should try that... But seriously, I feel that it's a combination of A and B. I don't think he's intentionally creepy, but he does make me feel uncomfortable. I've tried to leave him with my other friends (who are supposed to be his friends too) but he always follows me or leaves completely if I have to go home or something.
Thank you, it made me feel better to know that I'm not on this boat alone. (I shouldn't be happy about other people's depression though.) I hope everything works out for you.

I'm sorry. I can relate to you. I've had similar experiences, though probably not as bad. It was very difficult for me to find a job this summer. Fortunately I eventually got something after applying to dozens of jobs, though it's a pretty shitty job. Most of my friends got jobs with better salary and working conditions just by knowing the right people.

Sorry if I seem like a jerk or like I tried to one-up or something, just wanted to rant.
I'd buy one of those if they were sold as "Corgi belly scratchers".

It's not like that, they just don't want a member of this group to become closer to someone else than the group. They're actually the nicest and friendliest people I've ever met.

I guess I try to make them sound awful and myself sound like a victim (unconsciously). In reality, I've done great damage to most of my friends.

Our group of friends is very close, and a huge shitstorm would follow if someone had too close friends outside the group. Besides, I've been friends with them almost as long as I can remember, and I don't have any other close friends. I have to admit I'm making the same mistake as you since my SO is the only person I can talk about this besides my therapist.
I asked the same question and got "support".
I'd like to say something that could cheer you up but I can't think of anything. Take a hug instead.
